description: Engine-owned notification exclusions: marks survive ordinary checks until report retention ends, marking reports nothing, newly due early reports remain eligible, and a relaunch starts empty.

vectors.description: Asr is reported a second early. A clock-change mark half a second before its fire date excludes it across an ordinary update and resync; neither reports Asr again.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.6/§10.2–§10.3: the engine owns retained notification exclusions.

vectors.description: The engine has Asr in its schedule but hasn't reported it. Marking at a second before Asr doesn't check due alerts or exclude its future system request.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.6/§10.2–§10.3: the engine owns retained notification exclusions.

vectors.description: An explicit clock-change mark precedes Asr's first early report. The subsequent resync reports it, while a plan half a second before its fire date still includes it.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.6/§10.2–§10.3: the engine owns retained notification exclusions.

vectors.description: Asr is reported and marked, then the clock reaches exactly one day after its report without another update or resync. Querying ignores the expired mark.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.6/§10.2–§10.3: the engine owns retained notification exclusions.

vectors.description: Asr is reported and marked before a relaunch. The new engine has no report or mark to restore; a future Asr remains eligible. Report history records the old engine.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.6/§10.2–§10.3: the engine owns retained notification exclusions.
